title: Grateful Dead Live at Field House, Wesleyan University on 1970-05-03

ai_review.summary: A historically iconic Wesleyan concert with memorable moments, but captured on a very low‑fidelity audience tape that is often unlistenable.
ai_review.review: The recording is an amateur crowd‑mic capture – the mic even falls over at times and there’s abundant chatter, making the music difficult to hear.  Despite the poor audio, attendees recall a vivid anti‑war atmosphere, a surprise student composition played by Jerry, and highlights like China Cat Sunflower and Ron “Pigpen” McKernan’s organ work.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviewers rate the tape 0‑1 stars due to its terrible sound, but a few note historic and musical value, pulling the overall assessment slightly above the lowest tier.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Crowd microphone drops, frequent talk‑overs, low fidelity home‑brew mix; some reviewers note occasional clarity but overall muddy and unlistenable.

show_quality.setlist_flow: The concert featured an acoustic set (missing from this tape), a New Riders of the Purple Sage segment, then the Dead.  The evening was loosely organized with on‑stage announcements and spontaneous moments, reflecting the anti‑war protest atmosphere.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Played a student’s composition and contributed pedal steel during the NRPS set; guitar work not assessable due to recording quality.
band_member_comments.Keys: Ron "Pigpen" McKernan’s organ highlighted as a high point.
